videos.title: Roof Replacement Cost in Iowa City (2026) #iowacity #roofing
videos.headline: Roof Replacement Cost in Iowa City
videos.description:
How much does a new roof cost in Iowa City in 2026? A full residential roof replacement in the Iowa City area typically runs $7,840 to $19,600, with most standard-sized homes landing between $9,800 and $14,700. This pricing guide breaks down the price ranges, cost by home size, cost by roof type, how Iowa's hail, wind, ice and humidity affect your roof, storm damage and insurance, and the extra costs to plan for.

🔗 Iowa City roofing contractor:
https://www.michelcuevashome.com/

2026 roof replacement prices:
• Iowa statewide: $4,794 – $15,779 (average $6,160)
• Iowa City area, full replacement: $7,840 – $19,600
• Most standard-sized Iowa City homes: $9,800 – $14,700

Iowa roof cost by home size:
• 1,000 sq ft, 1 story: $7,226
• 1,500 sq ft, 1 story: $8,755
• 2,000 sq ft, 2 stories: $8,927
• 2,500 sq ft, 2 stories: $9,984
• 3,000 sq ft, 2 stories: $11,496
(The median Iowa home is 1,623 sq ft.)

Iowa roof cost by type (median-sized home):
• Asphalt shingles: $4.65/sq ft, about $4,794. Most popular and most affordable; lasts about 20–25 years
• Metal: $8.64/sq ft, about $8,911. Handles hail, wind and heavy snow; lasts 40+ years
• Wood shingles & shakes: $11.06/sq ft, about $11,401. Classic look, but humid summers can cause rot and mold
• Clay tile: $15.23/sq ft, about $15,703. Long-lasting, heavy, needs a specialist
• Slate: $15.30/sq ft, about $15,779. Top-of-the-line and the priciest
Class 4 impact-resistant asphalt shingles are rated for hail up to 2 inches and can qualify for insurance premium discounts.

How Iowa weather hits your roof:
• Spring hail: cracks shingles. Class 4 shingles hold up and can lower premiums
• Straight-line winds: lift shingles. Metal and wind-rated shingles hold on
• Ice dams: back water up under the eaves. Ice-and-water shield along eaves and valleys stops it
• Heavy snow: adds weight. Metal sheds snow and handles the load
• Freeze-thaw cycles: damage roof decking, which can add repair costs
• Humid summers: promote rot and mold. Good ventilation is a must

Storm damage: homeowners insurance often covers hail and wind damage, minus your deductible. Get the damage documented with photos and have your roofer meet the adjuster on-site.

Other costs to plan for: tear-off of the old roof (about 1.5 hours of labor per 100 sq ft), permits (most Iowa cities require one), rotted decking, and hidden damage (about 14% of homeowners said their final bill came in higher than their estimate).

Timing: the best time to reroof in Iowa is May through September. The average Iowa roof lasts 20–30 years. Iowa roofing prices run about 1–2% lower than Illinois and Wisconsin and about 12% lower than Minnesota.

videos.headline: What SEO Costs for a Window Film Company
videos.description:
How much does SEO and marketing cost for a window tinting or window film company in 2026? Most installers pay somewhere between $300 and $5,000 a month. This pricing guide breaks down the four tiers agencies charge, what you get at each level, how it compares to SEO pricing across all industries, what moves your price, and six questions to ask before you sign.

🔗 Window Film Marketing Agency:
https://windowfilmmarketingagency.com/

2026 window film SEO & marketing prices (per month):
• Starter: $300 – $500 (Google Business Profile management: categories, services, photos and posts; some on-site optimization)
• Growth: $500 – $1,000 (everything in Starter, plus citations on Yelp, Apple Maps, Bing and directories; analytics reporting; some backlinks)
• Multi-city: $1,000 – $2,000 (a page for every film type and service city; steady citations and backlinks; a review system that names the film; monthly reports on calls and estimate requests)
• Competitive market: $2,000 – $5,000 (for big, crowded markets: aggressive backlink building, citations everywhere buyers look, custom reporting by booked job, lead generation)

How that compares across all industries (SEO.com):
• Local SEO: $500 – $2,500 a month
• Traditional SEO: $1,500 – $5,000 a month
• Hourly SEO work: $75 – $200 an hour
• One-time projects: $1,000 – $30,000

What moves your price: your market (a big metro costs more than a small town), how many cities you serve, which film types you sell (residential, commercial, security, decorative, auto), your website's health, AI search visibility (often its own line item), and video and social media.

Is it worth it? One commercial window film lead can be a $20,000+ job. The top 3 on Google Maps get the calls. Profile fixes can help within weeks; rankings usually build over 3 to 6 months.

6 questions to ask before you sign:
1. Does it cover AI search like ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews?
2. Is software billed on top of the agency fee?
3. Do reports show calls and booked jobs, or just rankings?
4. Is it month-to-month?
5. Do I own my website and listings?
6. Do you work with my competitors?

videos.headline: Drain Cleaning Cost in Iowa City
videos.description:
How much does drain cleaning cost in Iowa City in 2026? Basic drain snaking starts at $120, no matter what, and runs up to about $250, depending on what has to be done and how easy the drain is to get to. This guide also covers what bigger jobs cost, prices by drain type, DIY vs. calling a pro, and the warning signs a drain needs cleaning.

🔗 Drain cleaning in Iowa City:
https://a1seweriowacity.com/drain-cleaning/

Iowa City basic drain snaking (2026):
• Starting price: $120, the bottom of the range no matter what
• Basic snaking: up to about $250
• Where you land depends on the job and the access to the drain

What other drain services cost (national averages):
• Basic snaking: $120 – $250
• Video camera inspection: $150 – $400
• After-hours emergency call: $150 – $500+
• Motorized auger: $200 – $350
• Hydro jetting: $300 – $600

Cost by drain type (national averages):
• Kitchen sink: $100 – $250
• Bathroom sink / shower: $100 – $225
• Toilet: $125 – $300
• Floor / laundry drain: $150 – $350
• Main sewer line: $250 – $600+

What moves your price: how bad the clog is, where it is and how easy it is to reach, the method (hand snake, cable machine, camera or hydro jetting), and timing. Many companies charge 1.5x to 2x after hours.

DIY vs. pro: a plunger ($5 – $15) or hand auger ($20 – $50) can handle shallow clogs. Chemical drain cleaners ($8 – $25) are hard on older pipes. Grease and roots need a cable machine or hydro jetting, and a camera shows what's in a line that keeps clogging.

Signs a drain needs cleaning: slow drains, a sink that fills while the dishwasher runs, a gurgling toilet or tub, a sewer smell near a floor drain, water coming up during a storm, or a clog that's back a week after plunging. One slow fixture usually means a local clog; several at once usually means the main line.

How much does it cost to install a new water heater in Iowa City in 2026? Most installs run from about $950 to $6,000. This pricing guide breaks down the cost of every system type, unit vs. labor, tank vs. tankless, what moves your price, and the signs it's time to replace.

🔗 Water heater installation in Iowa City:
https://a1seweriowacity.com/water-heater/

2026 average total installed cost (unit + labor):
• Electric tankless: $1,100 – $2,700
• Electric tank: $1,200 – $3,000
• Gas tank: $1,300 – $4,050
• Heat pump / hybrid: $2,000 – $6,300
• Gas tankless: $3,300 – $6,250

Unit vs. labor:
• Units run about $700 – $4,800
• Labor runs about $300 – $3,500
• Gas tankless costs the most to install: it usually needs a bigger gas line and different venting

Tank or tankless?
• Tank: lower upfront cost, usually a straight swap, hot water limited to what's in the tank
• Tankless: higher upfront cost, continuous hot water, mounts on the wall, often needs gas line and venting changes

What moves your price: the type and size of the unit, gas line upgrades, venting changes, and tight utility spaces.

Signs it's time to replace: water leaking from the bottom, rusty or discolored hot water, popping or rumbling sounds, hot water running out faster, or a tank over 10 years old. Most tanks last about 8 to 12 years. A leaking tank is an emergency.

Iowa tip: Eastern Iowa water is hard. Flush your tank now and then to slow scale buildup, and descale tankless units periodically. Ask your utility about rebates on efficient models.
